newsitem.title: KENYA: Zaire's Kengo will not attend summit - Kenya.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Kengo will not attend summit - Kenya.

text.p: Zairean Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo will not attend Tuesday's African summit on the conflict in eastern Zaire, Kenya's foreign minister said.
Foreign Minister Kalonzo Musyoka told Reuters at Nairobi airport: "No, he is not coming."

"Kengo has been given a dressing down in his parliament, (which was) suggesting that he may be an accomplice before and after the fact, which is why he may be taking a tough line," Musyoka said to explain Kengo's absence.
Kengo is half-Tutsi, which has placed him in a difficult political position after the lightning offensive by Tutsi-led rebels in eastern Zaire.

The presidents of Tanzania, Rwanda and Eritrea, the prime minister of Ethiopia and Burundi mediator Julius Nyerere, a former Tanzanian president, flew in on Tuesday morning for the summit, officials said.

Also expected were the presidents of Uganda and Zambia and Organisation of African Unity Secretary-General Salim Ahmed Salim. The foreign minister of Cameroon, current chairman of the OAU, is also due to take part in the talks.
Officials said the summit would start at 2 p.m. (1100 GMT).
